column2: ENGLISH

The banners of Chaos are torn down from the walls of Praag and burned in the square, and [Root.GetTitledFirstName] rides in through the broken gate. But the city is not the city it was. The stones are warm to the touch in winter. In the palace, in the merchants' halls, in the streets, faces have begun to push out of the walls, mouths open in a scream that makes no sound. The sorcerers of the north have left their mark on Praag, and it will not wash away. Strangely, the craftsmen of the city have never made finer work.
Ursun protect us. This is our city still.

[praag_mad.GetTitledFirstName] has stopped sleeping. At night they walk the corridors of the palace with a candle, stopping at every wall to listen, and in the morning they repeat to anyone who will hear what the stones told them. The servants are frightened. The physicians say it is the city.
Send them to the Ice Witches to be healed.
Everyone in Praag hears the walls. They will learn to stop listening.

A child of the court, [praag_mutant.GetFirstName], has begun to change. The midwives whisper that the curse of Praag gets into the young first. The marks are still small and could be hidden under a sleeve. For now.
Hide the child. No one needs to know.
Send the child north to the Ice Witches.
The Furnace takes what the curse has touched.

In the great hall the plaster has cracked in the night, and through the cracks the stone has pushed out into faces. Men and women and children, mouths open, eyes wide. One of them has the face of a servant who died last winter. Their lips move. If you stand close, you can almost hear what they are saying.
Call the priests of Ursun to pray over the hall.
Wall them over. New plaster, new paint, and no talk of it.
Lean close and listen.

In Praag the dead are burned, because in Praag the dead walk. The Furnace men are the ones who see to it, a grim brotherhood with iron hammers who stalk the graveyards at night and break whatever climbs out. Their master comes to [Root.GetTitledFirstName] with soot on his hands. The Furnace needs oil, coal and men, and the city has not paid for any of them in years.
Give them what they need. Ashes, not graves.
The Furnace will have to manage.

The bells of a whole district ring at once in the night. The dead have come up out of the cellars and the burial yards, more of them than anyone thought were buried there, and they are moving through the streets towards the living. The Furnace men cannot hold them alone.
Bring my hammer. I lead the Furnace men myself!
Pay the garrison to clear the streets.
Close the district and burn it, dead and all.

The Furnace men have caught one of the city's undertakers in a cellar with three corpses that should have been ash a month ago. The corpses were sitting up. The undertaker says he was only curious, and that he could be very useful to a lord who needed the dead to work.
Burn him in his own furnace.
Useful, you say? Bring him to court.
Drive him out of Praag.

The silversmiths of Praag have been the finest in Kislev for a thousand years, and they know it. Their guild master bows low before [Root.GetTitledFirstName] and unrolls a velvet cloth covered in drawings: chains, brooches, rings of filigree as fine as frost on a window. A piece for the lord of the city, he says, at a price for the lord of the city.
Commission the finest piece.
Not this year.

An old astronomer comes down from the Observatory, the tower where the first wizards of Praag watched the sky long before the Colleges of Altdorf were founded. He has been charting the stars over Kislev for forty years, he says, and they have begun to tell him things. With a little gold for new lenses, he will tell [Root.GetTitledFirstName] too.
Fund the readings.
Stars are for astronomers.

Servants have been going missing from the great houses of Praag. A kitchen girl here, a groom there, never from the same house twice. None of the boyars has reported it. Their stewards simply hire new ones. The city watch has noticed, and asks whether [Root.GetTitledFirstName] wishes them to look further.
Find out where they go.
Servants run off. Let it be.

The watch has a name. One boyar of the Duma never comes to the dawn prayers at the temple of Ursun, and has never been seen at a feast held in daylight. His servants go missing more often than anyone else's. His family has held its house in Praag for longer than anyone can remember.
Keep watching him.
Half the Duma sleeps through dawn prayers. Drop it.

An agent of [Root.GetTitledFirstName] gets into the boyar's house while he is away and finds the long gallery where the family portraits hang. The oldest one is of the boyar's great-grandfather, painted when Praag still had its first walls. It is the boyar. The same face, the same ring, the same grey streak in the beard. The agent comes back very pale.
Bring me everything you have.

It is the Upirnovs. They have lived in Praag for three hundred years and they have never once died. The blood of the von Carsteins runs cold in them, and they have fed on the city's servants for generations, quietly, carefully, never too many. Their head receives [Root.GetTitledFirstName] by candlelight and does not deny any of it. He only asks what it will take for this to remain between us.

It is the Kalashinivik sisters. Everyone in Praag knows them, the beautiful daughters of an old Duma house, and nobody has ever wondered why there are always beautiful daughters and never any mothers. They are Lahmians, sisters of Neferata's web, and half the secrets of the Duma pass through their salon. The eldest receives [Root.GetTitledFirstName] with a smile and asks what it will take for this to remain between us.
Nothing. The Circle of the Bear will burn the house tonight.
Gold, and secrets. And one of you serves at my court.
Tell me more about this blood.

A boyar of the Upirnov house comes to court, pale and courteous, with a soldier's bearing. Praag's streets are dangerous at night, he says, and he would be honoured to keep them quiet. He knows the city's gangs, its smugglers and its cellars better than any captain alive. He asks only that his work be done after dark.
Praag needs a man like you. Keep the peace.
I have captains enough.

A man of the Vasilikov family arrives in Praag with a chest of old charters, some so old the seals have crumbled. His house, he says, held the Uskovic quarter before the Tzarina's purge of the Praag nobility, and it was taken from them unjustly. He has the documents to prove it. He asks [Root.GetTitledFirstName] to recognise his claim.
The charters are good. Your claim is recognised.
Old paper means nothing. Go.
Seize him. I want to know who sent him.

The director of the Praag Opera House has a proposal. A new opera for the coming season, about the deeds of [Root.GetTitledFirstName], with the finest voices in Kislev and a chorus of a hundred. It will cost a great deal of gold. The librettist is brilliant, though he is known for a sharp pen.
Commission it. Let all Kislev hear of my reign.
I would rather not be sung about.

The season's prima donna is the talk of Praag. The boyars fight duels over her and the jewellers name brooches after her. She has made it known that she is looking for a patron, and that she would not mind if it were [Root.GetTitledFirstName].
Invite her to court.
Send flowers and a jewel to her dressing room.
I have no time for singers.

During the third act of the season's great opera, while the whole house watched the stage, a boyar was killed in his box. When the lights came up he was found sitting upright in his chair, white as paper, without a drop of blood left in him and two small wounds on his neck. The other boyars are leaving the city by the dozen.
Find out who did this.
Hush it up. Pay the right people.
Ungol knives. Everyone knows how they are.

Three times Praag tried to break away from the crown, until the Tzarina replaced its Z'ra rulers. The Z'ra never forgot. Now, with the crown of Kislev weak, a young man of the old line comes to [Root.GetTitledFirstName] by night, with Ungol atamans at his back. Praag was free once, he says. It could be free again, under a lord who stood with the Z'ra.
Praag stands with the Z'ra. We go our own way.
The crown will hear of this.
Go home, all of you, and I will forget this night.
Rebuild Cursed Praag
Pay masons and priests to rebuild the screaming walls of Praag with new stone. The curse will lift for twenty-five years, until it seeps back, or until Chaos takes the city again.
Curse of Praag
Praag was taken by Chaos and taken back, and the sorcerers' curse remains. Faces push out of the walls and minds give way, but the city's craftsmen have never worked finer.
Praag Rebuilt
New stone covers the screaming walls of Praag. For now, the curse is quiet.
Ashes Not Graves
The Furnace men are paid and busy. Praag's dead are burned, and the dead stay dead.
The Dead Walk
A district of the city was given up to the risen dead and burned.
The Upirnov Watch
An Upirnov boyar keeps the peace in Praag's streets at night. The streets are very quiet.
Hero of the Opera
An opera about this character's reign was the triumph of the Praag season.
Mocked at the Opera
An opera about this character's reign turned into a farce, and all Kislev is laughing.
Secrets of the Night
This character knows things that the dead have whispered.
Star Readings
The astronomers of the Praag Observatory read the stars for this character.
Betrayed the Z'ra
Warned me of the Z'ra
Championed the Z'ra
Blamed the Ungols
Furnace Hammer
An iron hammer of the Furnace men of Praag, black with soot. Its head is worn smooth from the skulls of the risen dead.

The stage-hands have found a door under the stage of the old opera house that was bricked up a century ago and is now open. Below it is a chamber painted with eight-pointed stars, still warm from candles, and a list of names. Several of them have seats in the boxes.
Raid it on the night of the next performance.
Let the Chekist deal with it quietly.
Close the opera house for the season.
The cult is broken, and the names on the list will not be seen at the opera again.
The chamber is empty when your men come. Someone warned them.
The Opera Cult
A Chaos cult was found under the Praag opera house.
The Opera Dark
The Praag opera house is closed for the season.
